Judgment

Both the appeals are filed by the claimants challenging the common judgment and award dated 02.03.2019, passed by the tribunal in MVC Nos.1024/2016 and MVC No.2292/2016 seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed on record.
3.
In this case, the factum of accident, death of deceased in the said accident and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

4. MFA No.103815/2019: In the present case, the tribunal awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
 Sl.No. Heads.

Amount in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependancy 7,14,000-00  2. Love and affection 60,000-00
3 . Funeral expenses 25,000-00
The deceased was aged 29 years as on the date of accident and was a bachelor died in the accident on 02.01.2016.
The accident is of the year 2016.
Hence notional income is to be taken at Rs.8,750-00 as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

sentences.text: There are totally 3 legal heirs.

Considering the age of the deceased,
the appropriate applicable multiplier is 17.
Therefore loss of dependency is re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.8,750/- +3500 (40% of 8,750/-) X 50% X 17 x 12 = Rs.12,49,500-00 6.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,
the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of NC: 2023:KHC-D:12386 consortium', along with 10% escalation.

7. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation' respectively, along with 10% escalation.
Therefore under these heads Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards loss of dependency 12,49,500-00  2. Towards loss of consortium 1,32,000-00

3 . Towards loss of estate and 33,000-00  transportation of dead body &
 funeral expenses.

Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,14,500-00 along with interest at NC: 2023:KHC-D:12386 the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.7,99,000-00 awarded by the tribunal.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
10. The claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 132 days in filing the appeal.

11. MFA NO.103817/2019:
The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimant, coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.
12.
In the present case, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the fracture of 5th and 6th ribs.
13. The tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.20,000/- along with interest at 9% per annum.
The claimant being 50 years old man doing agriculture work, certainly fracture of ribs causes/affects his earning capacity.
15. Further, claimant has suffered loss of enjoyment in life due to fracture of ribs.
Further, certain amount must have been spent towards medical expenses.
Therefore, considering all these facts, it is just and proper to award another sum of Rs.15,000/- in global in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal.

16. Therefore, the claimant is entitled for additional compensation of Rs.15,000/- in global in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal , along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from Shri.Mallikarjun S/O Rudrappa ... vs Smt.A.Anitha W/O V. 17. The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 132 days in filing the appeal.

18. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:12386 ORDER i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.
ii) The common judgments and award passed in MVC Nos.1024/2016 and MVC No.2292/2016 dated 02.03.2019 respectively, by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl.
MACT., Bailahongal are stands modified.
 iii) The claimants in MFA No.103815/2019 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,14,500-00 along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
iv) The claimant in MFA No.103817/2019 is entitled for additional compensation of Rs.15,000-00 in global in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:12386 v) The claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 132 days in filing the appeal respectively.
vi) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
vii) Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
viii) No order as to costs.
 ix) Draw award accordingly.
